newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices remain firm in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices remain firm in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices strengthened over this week's sales in Sydney, Geelong and Fremantle, Wesfarmers Dalgety said in its weekly market report.
"The market strengthened this week with prices rising for most types," Wesfarmers said.
The Eastern Market Indicator rose four cents to 626 cents a kg clean, while the western market indicator fell four cents since sales two weeks ago to 594 cents a kg .
A total of 78,916 bales were offered with a pass-in rate of 10.2 percent. The Wool International stockpile of unsold wool stands at 1,828,414 bales.
Trade competition was led by Japanese, Chinese and Western European buyers with support from most sectors of the trade.

Australian Council of Wool Exporters said exporters reported that the market held up well, with traditonal topmaking in Europe and the U.S. being responsible for the demand, but other sectors of the market, including China were relatively quiet.
The council said prices strengthened in the 20.5 micron and coarser wools, but there were less interest at the finer end, suggesting that commitments for finer wools may be nearing completion.

In the futures market, a total of 84 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract for the week ending 13 March. Open interest increased by 20 contracts to close at 840. The April 1997 contract rose two cents to 728 cents/kg clean.
Auction sales next week are in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with a total of 101,675 bales rostered for sale.
